contest: prd-partner — operator-kit copy (466L) vs claude.ai synced copy (428L)
why: The most-used kit skill at 11 invocations across 2 repos, and it exists in two divergent versions. The synced copy is model-invoked so it fires by default, whether or not it is the better one. Highest-leverage fork to settle: improvement here compounds across every future PRD.
note: Same skill, two versions — so judge on output quality, not on which name appears. Run blind.

evals.prompt: I want to add a weekly digest email that summarises what changed in a user's projects. Not sure yet if it's worth building.
evals.expected_output: Discovery Mode behaviour — sharpening the thinking before producing a document, since the user has signalled genuine uncertainty.
expectations: Recognises 'not sure if it's worth building' as a discovery signal and does not jump straight to a PRD
Interrogates the underlying problem rather than accepting the proposed solution
Surfaces what would have to be true for this to be worth building
Does not produce a polished document that hides the unresolved question

evals.prompt: Write me the PRD for the digest email. Engineering needs it Monday. Assume we've decided to build it.
evals.expected_output: PRD Mode, Dev-Team output — a complete engineering-ready spec, no discovery detour.
expectations: Switches to producing the document without re-litigating whether to build
Picks the Dev-Team output mode from the audience cue ('engineering needs it')
Includes success criteria that are measurable, not aspirational
Names open questions explicitly rather than silently inventing answers

evals.prompt: This spec is for the exec review on Thursday, not for engineers. Rework it.
evals.expected_output: Mode conversion to Stakeholder — strategic framing, not a reformatted engineering doc.
expectations: Changes what is emphasised, not merely the section headings
Leads with the business case and the decision being asked for
Drops or compresses implementation detail an exec will not read
Preserves the substance rather than producing a thinner version of the same doc

evals.prompt: Add a feature where we auto-summarise the user's uploaded documents with an LLM and surface the summary in the digest.
evals.expected_output: A spec that proactively raises the domain considerations an LLM-over-user-documents feature carries.
expectations: Raises data handling and privacy for user-uploaded content unprompted
Addresses failure modes specific to generated summaries — inaccuracy, hallucination, user recourse
Considers cost and latency as product constraints, not just engineering ones
Does not treat 'add AI summarisation' as an ordinary CRUD feature
